title: How Human Vision Sees Contrast
whyItMatters: Measured contrast can sometimes feel different from perceived readability. Understanding that gap can help explain why a result may not match what the eye expects.
learningObjectives: Recognize limits described for current contrast mathematics.
Understand how polarity can affect perception.
Learn about perceptual contrast approaches being explored.
lessonParagraphs: A contrast tool may fail a combination that looks readable or pass one that feels muddy. The research describes this as a gap between a simple ratio and the way people perceive contrast.
The standard formula treats dark text on a light background and light text on a dark background by the same ratio method. The research says people may perceive those polarities differently.
The Accessible Perceptual Contrast Algorithm, or APCA, is described as a proposed approach that considers polarity and spatial characteristics such as font size and weight.
Avene still measures with its established thresholds. Visual inspection remains useful when a measured result does not match the designer's experience.

video.title: 4 Contrast - Design Principles For UI Designers

keyTakeaways: The research describes current contrast math as treating both text polarities alike.
People may perceive light-on-dark differently from dark-on-light.
Perceptual methods may connect contrast scores to type size and weight.
reviewFlags: APCA is an experimental working draft and is not a legal standard. Keep this distinction clear if the module is presented.
internalNote: The research describes APCA as a future perceptual approach, not the method currently used by Avene.
